lessons.title: Introduction
lessons.content:
JavaScript is the most popular programming language in the world.

JavaScript is a programming language used to make web pages interactive.

JavaScript, often abbreviated to JS, is the default language of the internet. But it doesn’t stop there, JavaScript powers your smart TV, works with the Internet of Things, and helps build cross-platform apps.

➤	Why study JavaScript?
JavaScript is one of the 3 languages all web developers must learn:
	1.	HTML to define the content of web pages
	2.	CSS to specify the layout of web pages
	3.	JavaScript to program the behavior of web pages

➤	JavaScript Display Possibilities
JavaScript can "display" data in different ways:
	•	Writing into an HTML element, using innerHTML or innerText.
	•	Writing into the HTML output using document.write().
	•	Writing into an alert box, using window.alert().
	•	Writing into the browser console, using console.log().
lessons.example: JavaScript Display Example
lessons.content2:
➤Key Points:
	•	innerHTML / innerText → display inside an HTML element
	•	document.write() → writes directly to the webpage (use mainly for testing)
	•	window.alert() → shows a popup message to the user
	•	console.log() → displays output in the developer console (great for debugging)

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Variables
lessons.content:
Variables store data that can be used and changed in a program.

➤	Declaring Variables
In JavaScript, there are three ways to declare a variable:
	•	let vs const vs var
	•	let allows you to change the value later.
	•	const is used when the value should not change.
	•	var was used in older versions but is now less recommended.

➤	Variable Naming Rules
	•	Must start with a letter,_, or $.
	•	Cannot start with a number e.g. (let 1num = 5);.
	•	Case-sensitive (Name and name are different).
lessons.example:
Example:

let age = 25; //This value can be updated.

const pi = 3.14; //Cannot be changed.

var name = "Alice"; // Works, but not the best practice

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Strings
lessons.content: A string is a sequence of characters inside quotes.
lessons.example:
Example:

let text = "Hello, World!";

console.log(text.length); //Output: 13

console.log(text.toUpperCase()); //Outputs: HELLO, WORLD!

console.log(text.indexOf("World")); //Outputs:7

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Functions
lessons.content:
In JavaScript, a function is a reusable block of code that performs a specific task. It helps make your code cleaner, shorter, and easier to understand.

➤	Declaring a Function
To create a function, use the function keyword, followed by a name, parentheses () (with optional parameters), and curly braces { } for the code.
lessons.content2:
➤	Key Points:
	•	Functions use the function keyword.
	•	Code runs only when the function is called.
	•	return sends a value back.
	•	Parameters let you pass data into a function.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Conditions
lessons.content:
Conditions let your program make decisions.
They allow code to run differently depending on whether something is true or false.

➤	Declaring Conditions
You can use if, else if, and else statements to check values and run different code blocks.

Comparison Operators
➤	Operator & Meaning
==  Equal to (loose comparison)
===  Equal and same type (strict comparison)
!=  Not equal
<, >, <=, >=  Less than, greater than, etc.
➤	Common Errors & Mistakes
Using a single = instead of == or ===:
if (age = 18) {  // which results in error because a single = is used instead of == or ===
lessons.content2:
➤	Key Points:
	•	f checks a condition.
	•	else if runs if the first is false but this one is true.
	•	else runs when all are false.
	•	Comparison symbols:
			•	< less than
			•	> greater than
			•	== equal to

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Arrays
lessons.content:
An array is a special kind of variable that can hold many values at once.
Instead of creating many variables for different items, you can store them all together in one array.

It is very useful when you need to store lists such as names, numbers, or items.

➤	Declaring an Array
You can create an array by placing your values inside square brackets [ ], separated by commas.

➤	Accessing Array Elements
You can get any item from an array by using its index number inside square brackets.

➤	Changing an Array Element
You can change an existing item by using its index number.

➤	Array Length
Use the .length property to find out how many items are inside the array.
lessons.content2:
➤	Key Points:
	•	Arrays use square brackets [ ] to store multiple values.
	•	Each value in an array has a position number, called an index.
	•	The first item starts at index 0 (not 1).

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Objects
lessons.content:
An object in JavaScript is a type of variable that can store many related values together.

Instead of using numbers as positions like in arrays, objects use names (called keys or property names) to describe each value.

➤	Declaring an Object
You create an object using curly braces { }, and inside it, you write name–value pairs separated by commas.

	•	Each pair is called a property.
	•	The name part is called the key.
	•	The value part is the data stored in that property.

A car object can have:
				type: “Sedan”
				model: “Honda Civic LX”
				color: “Black”
lessons.content2:
➤	Key Points:
	•	An object holds data as name: value pairs.
	•	Property names are usually strings, and their values can be numbers, strings, arrays, booleans, or even other objects.
	•	You can have many properties inside one object, separated by commas.
	•	You can access property values using:
	•	Dot notation: objectName.propertyName
	•	Bracket notation: objectName["propertyName"]
	•	Objects can also contain functions, which are then called methods.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Loops
lessons.content:
A loop in JavaScript is used to repeat a block of code several times.

Instead of writing the same line again and again, a loop lets you run it automatically until a certain condition is met.
	•	A loop repeats a task as long as a condition is true.
	•	When the condition becomes false, the loop stops.

Types of Loops:
	1.	for loop – repeats a block of code a specific number of times
	2.	while loop – repeats as long as a condition is true
	3.	do…while loop – runs the code once, then checks the condition
lessons.content2:
➤	Key Points:
	•	Loops are used to repeat code automatically.
	•	Use break to stop a loop early.
	•	Use continue to skip one step in a loop.

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Classes:
lessons.content:
A class is like a blueprint for creating objects.
It defines what properties (data) and methods (actions) an object should have.

➤	Creating a Class
Use the class keyword followed by a name and curly braces { }.

➤	Constructor
The constructor is a special function inside a class.
It runs automatically when you create a new object from that class and is used to set up initial values.

➤	Getter (Computed Property)
A getter looks like a property but actually runs code to calculate a value.

➤	Methods
Methods are functions inside a class that make objects perform actions.
lessons.content2:
➤	Key Points:
•Class = Blueprint for objects
•Constructor = Initializes values
•this = Refers to the current object
•Getter = Calculates a value automatically
•Method = Function inside a class

lessons.title: Lesson 9: Modules:
lessons.content:
Modules help organize your JavaScript code by splitting it into smaller, reusable files.

Each file can export code and import it into another file.

➤	Exporting Code
Use the export keyword to share a function, class, or variable.

➤	Importing Code
Use the import keyword to bring code from another file.
lessons.content2:
➤	Key Points:
	•	export → shares code
	•	import → brings code in
	•	type="module" → tells browser to use modules
	•	Makes code clean, organized, and reusable

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Scope
lessons.content:
Scope defines where a variable or function can be used in your code.

➤	Global Scope
Variables declared outside any function can be used anywhere.

➤	Local Scope
Variables declared inside a function or block work only there.

➤	Block Scope (let and const)
let and const only work inside the block { } where they are declared.

➤	this Keyword
In a class, this refers to the current object.
If it loses meaning (like in an event), use .bind(this) or arrow functions.

➤	Arrow Functions and this
Arrow functions don’t create their own this, so they automatically use the correct one.
lessons.content2:
➤	Key Points:
	•	Global scope → accessible everywhere
	•	Local/block scope → inside { } only
	•	try...catch → handles errors safely
	•	this → current object reference
	•	Arrow functions → fix this scope issues

lessons.title: Lesson 11: Math
lessons.content:
The Math object provides built-in tools for calculations like square roots, angles, and distances.

➤	Vec Class Example
A vector represents a point or direction with x and y values.

➤	Finding Distance
Use the Pythagorean theorem to find distance between two points.

Finding Angles
Use Math.atan2(y, x) to find the angle of a vector in radians.

	•	Math.sqrt(x) → Square root
	•	Math.abs(x) → Absolute value
	•	Math.sin(x) → Sine (for Y movement)
	•	Math.cos(x) → Cosine 
	(for X movement)
	•	Math.atan2(y, x) → Finds angle
	•	Math.PI → π (3.1416)
lessons.content2:
➤	Key Points:
	•	Math helps with calculations
	•	Distance = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²)
	•	Angle = Math.atan2(y, x)
	•	Radians → Degrees = × 180 / π
	•	Used for movement, direction, and 
	animations

lessons.title: Lesson 12: JSON
lessons.content:
JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is a simple text format for storing and sharing data.
It’s easy for both humans and computers to read.

➤	Structure:
	•	{ } → Objects (key-value pairs)
	•	[ ] → Arrays (lists)

➤	Loading JSON with fetch()
Use fetch() to load data from a JSON file.

➤	Error Handling
Use .catch() to handle problems like missing data or typos.

➤	Finding Data in JSON
You can use array methods like reduce() to find specific information.
lessons.content2:
➤	Key Points:
	•	JSON = Data format for sharing info
	•	{ } = Objects, [ ] = Arrays
	•	fetch() = loads JSON
	•	.then() = runs after success
	•	.catch() = handles errors
	•	reduce() = finds one result 
	(like largest/smallest)
